title: Differences in anti-viral immune responses in individuals of Indian and European origin: relevance for the COVID-19 pandemic
authors: Geckin B; Zoodsma M; Kilic G; Debisarun PA; Rakshit S; Adiga V; Ahmed A; Parthiban C; Kumar NC; D’Souza G; Baltissen MP; Martens JHA; Andres JD; Li Y; Vyakarnam A; Netea MG
one_liner_zh: 该文比较印度与欧洲人群的抗病毒免疫反应差异，聚焦染色质可及性与细胞因子产生，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, large differences in susceptibility and mortality due to SARS-CoV-2 infection have been reported between populations in Europe and South Asia. While both host and environmental factors (including BCG vaccination) have been proposed to explain this, the potential biological substrate of these differences is unknown. We purified peripheral blood mononuclear cells from individuals living in India and the Netherlands at baseline and 10-12 weeks after BCG vaccination. We compared chromatin accessibility between the two populations at baseline, as well as gene transcription profiles and cytokine production capacities upon viral stimulation with influenza and SARS-CoV-2. The chromatin accessibility of genes important for adaptive immunity was higher in Indians compared to Europeans, while the latter had more accessible chromatin regions in genes of the innate immune system. At the transcriptional level, we observed that Indian volunteers displayed a more tolerant immune response to viral stimulation, in contrast to a more exaggerated response in Europeans. BCG vaccination strengthened the tolerance program in Indians, but not in Europeans. These differences may partly explain the different impact of COVID-19 on the two populations.
abstract_zh: 在COVID-19疫情期间，欧洲与南亚人群之间因SARS-CoV-2感染导致的易感性和死亡率存在显著差异。尽管已有研究提出宿主因素和环境因素（包括BCG疫苗接种）可能解释这一现象，但这些差异的潜在生物学基础尚不明确。我们采集了印度和荷兰个体在基线及BCG疫苗接种后10-12周的外周血单核细胞，比较了两组人群在基线的染色质可及性，以及流感病毒和SARS-CoV-2刺激后的基因转录谱和细胞因子产生能力。与欧洲人相比，印度人在适应性免疫相关基因的染色质可及性更高，而欧洲人在先天免疫系统基因中具有更多可及的染色质区域。在转录水平上，我们观察到印度志愿者对病毒刺激表现出更耐受的免疫反应，而欧洲人则表现出更强烈的反应。BCG疫苗接种增强了印度人的耐受程序，但在欧洲人中未观察到这一效果。这些差异可能部分解释了COVID-19对两个人群的不同影响。
